draft.title: Peasants, workers and the Great Fear
card: In 1788 and 1789, poor harvests pushed up the price of bread. Bread was the main food of poor families, so many Parisian workers went hungry and angry.
In the countryside, peasants still paid dues and taxes to lords and the church. In mid-1789 many peasants attacked noble estates, and some burned records of the dues they owed.
Rumours spread that nobles had hired armed men to crush the peasants. Fear moved quickly from village to village and led to more attacks. This panic is called the Great Fear.
These actions came from ordinary people, not from the Assembly. They showed that the revolution could not be controlled from above, and they pushed the new National Assembly to act on privilege.
draft.remember: Hunger and anger among workers and peasants moved the revolution beyond politicians.

a.q: Why was the Great Fear important to the course of the revolution?
opts: Peasant action put pressure on the Assembly to end privilege
It was a plan by the Assembly to remove the king from power
It ended the unrest as peasants began to trust their lords
It began when the Estates-General first voted by head
a.why: Attacks on estates and fear across the countryside showed that ordinary people were acting on their own. This pressured the Assembly to deal with privilege. The Assembly did not plan it, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Who acted in the Great Fear, and who then had to respond?

b.q: In July 1789, villagers near Lyon burn the records of dues they owe to a local lord after hearing a rumour of hired armed men. What does this best show?
opts: Peasants acted on their own grievances and fears
The Assembly had ordered peasants to attack nobles
Bread prices had fallen, so peasants felt confident
Nobles had given up their dues of their own free will
b.why: Burning the records targets the dues peasants resented, and the rumour of armed men shows the fear that drove the Great Fear. Both point to action by peasants themselves. The Assembly did not order these attacks, so the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about who started the attacks and what they were angry about.

a.best: Peasant action put pressure on the Assembly to end privilege

b.best: Peasants acted on their own grievances and fears
